visual.general_description: Color photograph or scan of a 12-lead electrocardiogram printed on pink grid paper.
visual.detailed_description: A 12-lead ECG on pink millimetre-style grid paper with a lighter dotted fine grid. Four rows of tracing are visible. Lead labels printed in the image are I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF, V1, V2, V3, V4, V5 and V6, arranged in four columns with the printed labels I, II and III at the left of rows one to three, and a bottom row labelled II that runs across the full width. A rectangular calibration pulse appears at the left end of each of the four rows. Some tall deflections in the precordial leads extend past the top edge of the image. A strip of printed text along the top edge is cut off and not legible. No patient name, panel letter or numeric overlay other than the lead labels is legible.

visual.general_description: Three grayscale coronary angiogram frames labelled LAD, LCX and RCA.
visual.detailed_description: Three square grayscale X-ray angiography frames side by side. The left frame is labelled LAD at its lower left, the middle frame LCX and the right frame RCA, each printed in white text. Each frame shows a dark contrast-filled coronary artery with branches against a lighter background of lung and cardiac shadow; the LAD and LCX frames show a tree of branching vessels descending from the upper part of the frame, and the RCA frame shows a vessel with a looping course toward the right and a catheter-like line entering from the top. No panel letters, arrows, scale bars, patient names or dates are legible.
